title: Spelling counts where the word is taught
statement: Count spelling only where the word itself was taught: a taught word recalled from memory must be spelled exactly; elsewhere a slip is named but not marked wrong.
example: In a sentence said back, a slip is named and passed only in a key word of five letters or more.
detail: Both rules came over from a 3D version's marking, and both run in code. The key-word deck takes an exact match, does not count another deck word that fits the sentence as a miss, and meets a near spelling with 'Nearly. That is the word, but the spelling is not right yet.', since a taught word is spelled right; the second miss gives the word. The say-it-back task checks that every key word is there and names a slip in a word of five letters or more without counting it as a miss.
against: An animated version's export asks the key words as one gap answered by a choice, so spelling is not checked there (`g9/transformer/src/glue/animated.js`, line 152).
